question: Where does each VCFcache engine generation stand against each annotator's own uncached run, at panel/WES/WGS, with fixed cost and per-variant cost separated?
sample: LP6005519-DNA_A06 (SGDP, GRCh38) for the annotator matrix; KPGP-00319 for the heavy VEP rungs
harness: benchmarks/adaptive_routing.py, one Slurm step per cell, complete-record audit outside timing

arms.direct: uncached annotation, the reference every cached arm is audited against
arms.legacy: legacy engine as it stands on feature/native-bcf-routing 63757a07
arms.auto: adaptive engine, 8830bf7b3 lineage, labelled 'adaptive' in the summary

jobs.status: ABORTED: driver stopped at the first audit failure; superseded by 1315
FAILED: srun step launch on sl-w5 returned 167, 'Job credential expired'; node excluded thereafter; superseded by 1316
CANCELLED before its cached arms so the audit-tolerant driver could be used; superseded by 1317

jobs.what: VEP everything, assay scales, 6 arms, 16 cpus

jobs.status: FAILED: passed arm name 'adaptive'; the driver calls it 'auto'; failed at argument parsing, no cluster time used; superseded by 1320
FAILED: same arm-name error; superseded by 1321

jobs.what: heavy VEP everything+500us/consequence, KPGP-00319 WGS, main/adaptive/native, 8 cpus

jobs.status: CANCELLED by request after 2h19m with no cells: each arm costs ~2.25h and the result was already bounded to <=1.018x by the cache-side budget

reused_without_rerun.why: the 500us and 10ms uncached arms cost 4.2 h and 22.7 h; the 500us rung was re-anchored with a fresh main cell measured in the same job at the campaign's 8 cpus / 8 vep_forks
reused_without_rerun.anchor_agreement: fresh main 1796.21 s vs archived 1805.37 s, 0.5%

known_output_discrepancies.vep: HGNC_ID differs at 2/82714 (WES) and 28/4858092 (WGS) records; Ensembl/ensembl-vep#1959: merge_features back-fills HGNC IDs by gene symbol from other features in the same annotation buffer, so the value depends on buffer composition and any subset annotation can differ from a full-input run; identical in all five cached arms
known_output_discrepancies.veprs-clinical: ClinVar-derived CSQ differs at 22/82714 (WES) and 40/4858092 (WGS) records; cause not established; identical in all five cached arms
known_output_discrepancies.engine_independence: every cached arm reported byte-identical mismatch counts and loci, so routing is not implicated in either case

limitations: one run per cell; observed run-to-run spread was 1-3% (VEP WES uncached 273.98 s in job 1301 vs 282.33 s in 1315)
differences of a few percent between engine arms are not evidence of an ordering
no cross-annotator comparison is valid: the annotators do different work and vep-rs in particular differs in behaviour
the heavy rungs use a different sample and a different CPU count (8) than the annotator matrix (16)
main at 136bafa9 lacks the --engine option, so its arm omits that flag; all other arms pass it
